name: teamtype
desc: Peer-to-peer, editor-agnostic collaborative editing of local text files
why: Peer-to-peer, editor-agnostic collaborative editing is a neat look at how real-time sync works without a server.

brief.what_it_is: Teamtype is a command-line daemon, `teamtype`, that gives you real-time collaborative editing of plain local text files without a server. You run `teamtype share` in a directory, and another person runs `teamtype join` with the printed join code in their own directory. Edits sync between the two directories, and you edit through your usual editor via a plugin (Neovim, VS Code/Codium, or a community plugin for JetBrains, TeXstudio, and others). Peers see each other's cursors, selections, and edits, and it works on whole directories, not just single files.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as the missing real-time complement to Git and other version control systems, aimed at pair programming, brainstorming, and note-taking. The project says it is built by people who want to use it themselves and share it with others, and that it is not a company and has nothing to sell.
brief.how_it_works: Two peers connect over encrypted peer-to-peer connections, with no server required, and the content stays on disk so you keep full access even offline (a local-first model). The README credits Automerge, Iroh, and Magic Wormhole as the underlying pieces. Editors talk to the local daemon through a simple JSON-RPC protocol, which is what plugin authors implement. The README does not go deeper on the sync mechanism beyond these pointers.

commands_seen.context: Run in the directory you want to share; prints a join code such as 5-hamburger-endorse and reports when a peer connects.
Run by the other person in a separate directory (works on the same machine too) using the join code; stores the peer's address in .teamtype/config and connects.
Homebrew install of the teamtype command, listed under the Homebrew tab of the README installation section.
Arch Linux install of the teamtype package.
Gentoo install; the README says to enable the GURU repository first.
Nix: puts teamtype on PATH temporarily for the current shell.
Builds teamtype from source via Cargo.
Installs a precompiled binary from the latest release using cargo-binstall, to skip compiling.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install: the README lists precompiled static binaries on GitHub releases (x86_64-linux-static for Linux, universal-apple-darwin for macOS, aarch64-aarch64-linux-static for Android via Termux), plus Arch, Gentoo, Nix, and Cargo routes. Windows is supported only through WSL. You also need an editor plugin: the Neovim plugin (teamtype-nvim) or the 'Teamtype' extension from the VS Code/Codium marketplace. Make sure teamtype is on PATH when the editor launches. No account is required. Joining writes peer config into .teamtype/config in the directory, and the README warns that this overwrites any previous config there.
brief.standout: Peer-to-peer and editor-agnostic at once: there is no server and no account, and any editor with a plugin (or a bridge like the LSP or Hedgedoc prototypes) can join the same session. It was renamed from Ethersync in October 2025, so older posts and talks may use the old name.
brief.status: Maintained, with a caveat. The README says the team maintains it in their free time, that they use it for their own pair programming, and that there are open bugs. Funding came from NLnet NGI0 Core in 2024 and the Prototype Fund in 2025. I did not see a release date or last commit date in the pages I read, so the activity level is only inferred from the README.
brief.caveats: Windows is supported only via WSL. Android is reachable only through a terminal emulator like Termux. The README says there are bugs to be aware of, and the project is maintained in spare time. Licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later, so embedding it carries those obligations. CONTRIBUTING.md has a 'strict no-LLM policy' that contributors must follow. The docs homepage ends with a wry line about 'What to learn from us' for people who find it 'after Teamtype has died'. Joining overwrites the existing .teamtype/config in that directory. The homepage I fetched was only the mdBook introduction; the real install and usage content is in the GitHub README.
quotes: Multiplayer mode for your text editor!
It's the missing real-time complement to Git and other version control systems!
We are not a company and do not have anything to sell.
